gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured capacity for any D-size NiMH cell. The only lab test of a major-brand D rechargeable in this research is lygte-info's (HKJ). It found that Energizer's NH50 D delivers its rated 2,500 mAh, which is a quarter of the 10,000 mAh the recommended cells claim, and that the cell has a smaller cell inside a D-size shell.
standout_why: I compared against New World Survival (cited), Reactual (cited), Popular Science (cited), The Prepared (cited) and Michael Bluejay's NiMH guide. New World Survival lists only maker ratings and says there is 'no independent testing lab publishing head-to-head comparisons' for D cells. Michael Bluejay says 'Capacity is mfr. claimed, not from independent testing.' Popular Science and The Prepared give no measured D figures. Reactual says, with no number, that Energizer's D rechargeables are 'AA cells repackaged in a D-sized shell.' So the warning already exists in a rival, and ChatGPT's answer repeats it. What none of them has is a named lab's measured figure. No measurement of the actual picks (Tenergy Centura, Tenergy Premium, EBL, Powerex) could be sourced from an opened page.
decides: The finding backs ChatGPT's 'buy true D cells, avoid AA-inside cells' advice with a lab number: a 2,500 mAh measured cell against 8,000–10,000 mAh full-size cells. It does not choose between Tenergy, EBL and Powerex. The only named first-hand reports on Tenergy's 10,000 mAh line are from Budget Light Forum users in 2016: flydiver called the blue cells inconsistent and expected about 8,000 mAh from the Premiums, and Zebretta measured high internal resistance. That argues against trusting the 10,000 mAh labels, but it is not a measured capacity.

findings.label: Lab-measured capacity vs rating (lygte-info / HKJ)
findings.value: Delivers its rated 2,500 mAh (rated at 500 mA to 1.0 V, 21 °C)
findings.note: HKJ's text says: 'The two cells matches fairly well and can deliver the rated capacity.' The measured mAh values are in chart images only, and the page shows no review date. 2,500 mAh is 25% of a 10,000 mAh label.

findings.label: Construction and weight (lygte-info / HKJ)
findings.value: Smaller cell inside a D shell; 73.0 g typical weight
findings.note: HKJ: 'they contain a smaller cell inside' and 'These batteries do not have more capacity than AA batteries, but are better at high current.' The 73.0 g weight is the maker's typical-weight figure, quoted on the page.

findings.product: Tensai D TR-D10000 (Tenergy sister brand), reference full-size 10,000 mAh D
findings.label: Lab-tested full-size D cell (lygte-info / HKJ), weight for comparison
findings.value: Rated 10,000 mAh typical / 9,000 mAh minimum; 163 g
findings.source_title: Test/Review of Tensai D TR-D10000 10000mAh (Green) – BudgetLightForum
findings.note: HKJ posted this on 2013-10-19. The measured results are only in chart images; in his conclusion he writes 'I do like the 10Ah capacity.' The 163 g is the official spec, not a measurement. In the comments, HKJ says he has not tested the Tenergy D, so he can't say whether it is the same cell. The 163 g vs 73 g difference shows the full-cell vs small-cell gap by weight.

findings.label: Internal resistance measured by forum user Zebretta
findings.value: 80, 92, 89 and 102 (presumably mΩ) new, later about 50–60 mΩ after cycling
findings.source_title: Resistance values of new Tenergy 10000mAh D-Cells – BudgetLightForum
findings.note: Posted 2016-12-16. Cells were charged on an iMax B6 mini at 1.0 A for 16 h after discharge to 0.9 V; the meter was not named. HKJ, replying in the thread, called the initial values 'way to high.' This covers the blue-label line, not the Premium (white) or Centura.

findings.label: Named first-hand judgement (BudgetLightForum user flydiver)
findings.value: Blue 10K cells 'all over the place for consistency and capacity'; Premium D 'none will HAVE 10K capacity', '~8K, functionally'
findings.note: Posted 2016-12-13. These are qualitative judgements with no mAh test figures. In the same thread, flydiver says Tenergy Centura 5K C cells 'do live up to the capacity claim' (C size, not D).

unsourced: Measured capacity (mAh or Wh) for Tenergy Centura D 8000, Tenergy Premium D 10000, EBL D 10000, Powerex MH-DP100 and Amazon Basics D. I looked for RTINGS-style lab tests, lygte-info's D index (it covers only Ansmann, Varta, Energizer, Tensai and Panasonic Pro Power D), BudgetLightForum and CandlePowerForums threads, and searches by model name.

A BatteryJunction customer review said to report a Tenergy Premium 10105 D at 10,081 mAh (1.13662 Ω resistor, 13 h 45 m). The page returned HTTP 429 on both tries, so the reviewer name, date and figure are unverified.

Tenergy Centura D figures of 8,041 and 8,346 mAh (BM200 charger, 500 mA discharge) appeared only in a search summary. The BudgetLightForum thread I opened does not contain them, and an exact-number search found no source.
The CandlePowerForums thread 'Dischrging/Charging Tenergy 10000 mah D Cells' returned HTTP 403, so its user-measured mAh values could not be read.
The SF Approved 2016 recommended-D-batteries PDF (a ChatGPT result) could not be text-extracted, so I could not check whether it lists measured capacities.
Measured self-discharge (charge retention after storage) for any of the D candidates. I found only maker claims (85% after one year for Tenergy and Powerex, 80% after three years for EBL).
